title: Are you ready for your exam
paragraphs: So, it's exam time again — have you done the necessary work to get good marks? Sleeping with the textbook under the pillow in the hope that knowledge will be magically absorbed into your brain as you sleep doesn't work. The best strategy is to space your practice out, rather than cram it all together. It means hit the books early!

In an article in the British newspaper The Guardian, Tom Stafford, a lecturer in psychology and cognitive science at the University of Sheffield, UK, advises: "If you organise five hours of study into one hour a day, you'll remember more than if you study for five hours on one day." Don't rely on memory alone — get pen and paper and start working. Students who can test themselves in advance will be better at retrieving material from their memory and learn that material in the long run. John Dunlosky, Professor of Psychology at Kent State University in the US, suggests that "you start by reading a textbook using your favourite highlighter and favourite colours, but then you go back and make flashcards of all the critical concepts and instead of just rereading those, you basically try to test yourselves on them."

Good revision should give you confidence, but if you are still anxious, there's no harm in indulging in a personal ritual. In Japan, it seems to be a tradition for students to eat Katsudon before a test. This is a warm bowl of rice topped with egg and a deep-fried pork cutlet. The name of the dish reminds people of the word 'katsu', meaning 'winning'.

For some students in South Korea, the key to success is not washing their hair before sitting an exam because they believe they could wash all the knowledge out of their head. And in different parts of the world there are always those who swear by their 'lucky underwear'.
The bottom line is that you need to study, sleep well on the eve of the test, eat a nutritious meal, drink plenty of water and believe that your efforts will pay off. Good luck in your exam!

vocabulary.entry: exam time [n.] /ɪɡˈzæm taɪm/ 考试时间 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Exam time is stressful for most students.
vocabulary.translation: 考试时间对大多数学生来说压力很大。

vocabulary.entry: necessary [adj.] /ˈnesəsəri/ 必要的；必需的
vocabulary.example: Sleep is necessary for good health.
vocabulary.translation: 睡眠对健康是必要的。

vocabulary.entry: get good marks [phr.] /ɡet ɡʊd mɑːks/ 取得好成绩 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: She studies hard to get good marks.
vocabulary.translation: 她努力学习以取得好成绩。

vocabulary.entry: textbook [n.] /ˈtekstbʊk/ 教科书；课本
vocabulary.example: The textbook was too expensive for some students.
vocabulary.translation: 这本教科书对一些学生来说太贵了。

vocabulary.entry: magically [adv.] /ˈmædʒɪkli/ 如魔法般地；神奇地
vocabulary.example: The problem did not magically disappear.
vocabulary.translation: 问题并没有神奇地消失。

vocabulary.entry: absorb into [phr.] /əbˈzɔːb ˈɪntə/ 吸收；并入 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The body absorbs nutrients into the bloodstream.
vocabulary.translation: 身体将营养物质吸收到血液中。

vocabulary.entry: strategy [n.] /ˈstrætədʒi/ 策略；战略
vocabulary.example: We need a new strategy to win the game.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要一个新的策略来赢得比赛。

vocabulary.entry: space out [phr.] /speɪs aʊt/ 把……间隔开 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Space out your study sessions to avoid burnout.
vocabulary.translation: 把你的学习时段间隔开以避免过度疲劳。

vocabulary.entry: cram [v.] /kræm/ 临时死记硬背；填塞
vocabulary.example: He stayed up all night cramming for the exam.
vocabulary.translation: 他熬了一整夜为考试临时抱佛脚。

vocabulary.entry: hit the books [phr.] /hɪt ðə bʊks/ 开始用功读书 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: I need to hit the books if I want to pass.
vocabulary.translation: 如果我想通过考试，就需要开始用功读书了。

vocabulary.entry: lecturer [n.] /ˈlektʃərə/ 讲师
vocabulary.example: The lecturer spoke clearly about the topic.
vocabulary.translation: 讲师清楚地讲述了这个话题。

vocabulary.entry: psychology [n.] /saɪˈkɒlədʒi/ 心理学
vocabulary.example: She is studying psychology at university.
vocabulary.translation: 她在大学学习心理学。

vocabulary.entry: cognitive science [n.] /ˈkɒɡnətɪv ˈsaɪəns/ 认知科学 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Cognitive science combines psychology and neuroscience.
vocabulary.translation: 认知科学结合了心理学和神经科学。

vocabulary.entry: organise [v.] /ˈɔːɡənaɪz/ 组织；安排 (英式拼写，美式: organize)
vocabulary.example: He organised the files alphabetically.
vocabulary.translation: 他按字母顺序整理了文件。

vocabulary.entry: rely on [phr.] /rɪˈlaɪ ɒn/ 依赖；依靠 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Don't rely on luck; prepare well.
vocabulary.translation: 不要依赖运气，要好好准备。

vocabulary.entry: retrieve [v.] /rɪˈtriːv/ 检索；取回 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The dog retrieved the ball from the water.
vocabulary.translation: 狗从水中叼回了球。

vocabulary.entry: in the long run [phr.] /ɪn ðə lɒŋ rʌn/ 从长远来看 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Exercise pays off in the long run.
vocabulary.translation: 从长远来看，锻炼是有回报的。

vocabulary.entry: highlighter [n.] /ˈhaɪlaɪtə/ 荧光笔
vocabulary.example: She used a yellow highlighter to mark key points.
vocabulary.translation: 她用黄色荧光笔标记重点。

vocabulary.entry: flashcard [n.] /ˈflæʃkɑːd/ 抽认卡
vocabulary.example: He made flashcards to learn vocabulary.
vocabulary.translation: 他制作了抽认卡来学习词汇。

vocabulary.entry: critical [adj.] /ˈkrɪtɪkəl/ 关键的；重要的
vocabulary.example: This is a critical step in the process.
vocabulary.translation: 这是过程中关键的一步。

vocabulary.entry: reread [v.] /ˌriːˈriːd/ 再读；重读
vocabulary.example: He reread the letter to make sure he understood.
vocabulary.translation: 他重读了那封信以确保自己理解了。

vocabulary.entry: revision [n.] /rɪˈvɪʒən/ 复习；修订 (英式英语)
vocabulary.example: Revision is essential before final exams.
vocabulary.translation: 期末考试前复习是必不可少的。

vocabulary.entry: anxious [adj.] /ˈæŋkʃəs/ 焦虑的；担忧的
vocabulary.example: She felt anxious about the interview.
vocabulary.translation: 她对面试感到焦虑。

vocabulary.entry: indulge in [phr.] /ɪnˈdʌldʒ ɪn/ 沉迷于；尽情享受 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: He indulged in a piece of chocolate cake.
vocabulary.translation: 他尽情享用了一块巧克力蛋糕。

vocabulary.entry: ritual [n.] /ˈrɪtʃuəl/ 习惯做法；仪式
vocabulary.example: Her morning coffee is a daily ritual.
vocabulary.translation: 她早上的咖啡是每日习惯。

vocabulary.entry: Katsudon [n.] /ˈkætsudɒn/ 猪排盖饭 (日语借词)
vocabulary.example: Katsudon is a popular dish in Japan.
vocabulary.translation: 猪排盖饭在日本是一道受欢迎的菜。

vocabulary.entry: top with [phr.] /tɒp wɪð/ 在……上面加 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Top the pizza with cheese and olives.
vocabulary.translation: 在披萨上面加奶酪和橄榄。

vocabulary.entry: deep-fried [adj.] /ˌdiːp ˈfraɪd/ 油炸的
vocabulary.example: Deep-fried food is high in calories.
vocabulary.translation: 油炸食品热量很高。

vocabulary.entry: pork cutlet [n.] /pɔːk ˈkʌtlət/ 猪排
vocabulary.example: He ordered a pork cutlet with rice.
vocabulary.translation: 他点了一份猪排饭。

vocabulary.entry: remind of [phr.] /rɪˈmaɪnd əv/ 使想起 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The song reminds me of my childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 这首歌使我想起了我的童年。

vocabulary.entry: sit an exam [phr.] /sɪt ən ɪɡˈzæm/ 参加考试 (英式英语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: She sat the exam in June.
vocabulary.translation: 她在六月参加了考试。

vocabulary.entry: swear by [phr.] /sweə baɪ/ 深信；信赖 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: He swears by this method for learning English.
vocabulary.translation: 他对这种学英语的方法深信不疑。

vocabulary.entry: bottom line [n.] /ˈbɒtəm laɪn/ 关键；要点 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The bottom line is that we need more time.
vocabulary.translation: 关键是我们需要更多时间。

vocabulary.entry: eve [n.] /iːv/ 前夕；前夜
vocabulary.example: On the eve of the wedding, she was nervous.
vocabulary.translation: 婚礼前夕，她很紧张。

vocabulary.entry: nutritious [adj.] /njuːˈtrɪʃəs/ 有营养的；营养丰富的
vocabulary.example: Eat a nutritious breakfast every day.
vocabulary.translation: 每天吃一顿有营养的早餐。

vocabulary.entry: pay off [phr.] /peɪ ɒf/ 取得成功；得到回报 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: All his hard work paid off in the end.
vocabulary.translation: 他所有的努力最终得到了回报。

sentences.english: So, it's exam time again — have you done the necessary work to get good marks?
sentences.chinese: 所以，又到考试时间了——你有没有为取得好成绩做必要的准备呢？

sentences.english: Sleeping with the textbook under the pillow in the hope that knowledge will be magically absorbed into your brain as you sleep doesn't work.
sentences.chinese: 把课本放在枕头底下睡觉，指望睡觉时知识能神奇地被大脑吸收，这是行不通的。

sentences.english: The best strategy is to space your practice out, rather than cram it all together.
sentences.chinese: 最好的策略是把你的学习时间分散开，而不是把所有的学习任务都集中在一起。

sentences.english: It means hit the books early!
sentences.chinese: 这意味着要早点开始用功读书！

sentences.english: In an article in the British newspaper The Guardian, Tom Stafford, a lecturer in psychology and cognitive science at the University of Sheffield, UK, advises: "If you organise five hours of study into one hour a day, you'll remember more than if you study for five hours on one day."
sentences.chinese: 在英国《卫报》的一篇文章中，英国谢菲尔德大学心理学和认知科学讲师汤姆·斯塔福德建议道：“如果你把五个小时的学习时间安排成每天一小时，那么你记住的内容会比一天学习五个小时记住的更多。”

sentences.english: Don't rely on memory alone — get pen and paper and start working.
sentences.chinese: 不要仅仅依赖记忆——拿出笔和纸，开始学习吧。

sentences.english: Students who can test themselves in advance will be better at retrieving material from their memory and learn that material in the long run.
sentences.chinese: 能够提前自我测试的学生将更善于从记忆中检索信息，并且从长远来看，他们能更好地掌握这些知识。

sentences.english: John Dunlosky, Professor of Psychology at Kent State University in the US, suggests that "you start by reading a textbook using your favourite highlighter and favourite colours, but then you go back and make flashcards of all the critical concepts and instead of just rereading those, you basically try to test yourselves on them."
sentences.chinese: 美国肯特州立大学心理学教授约翰·邓洛斯基建议：“你可以先用你最喜欢的荧光笔和喜欢的颜色阅读课本，然后回过头来，把所有关键概念做成抽认卡，不要只是重读这些概念，而要从根本上尝试对自己进行测试。”

sentences.english: Good revision should give you confidence, but if you are still anxious, there's no harm in indulging in a personal ritual.
sentences.chinese: 良好的复习应该能给你信心，但如果你仍然感到焦虑，沉迷于个人仪式也无妨。

sentences.english: In Japan, it seems to be a tradition for students to eat Katsudon before a test.
sentences.chinese: 在日本，学生们在考试前吃猪排盖饭似乎是一种传统。

sentences.english: This is a warm bowl of rice topped with egg and a deep-fried pork cutlet.
sentences.chinese: 这是一碗热腾腾的米饭，上面盖着鸡蛋和炸猪排。

sentences.english: The name of the dish reminds people of the word 'katsu', meaning 'winning'.
sentences.chinese: 这道菜的名字让人联想到“katsu”这个词，意思是“胜利”。

sentences.english: For some students in South Korea, the key to success is not washing their hair before sitting an exam because they believe they could wash all the knowledge out of their head.
sentences.chinese: 对于一些韩国学生来说，成功的关键是在参加考试前不洗头，因为他们认为洗头会把脑子里的知识都洗掉。

sentences.english: And in different parts of the world there are always those who swear by their 'lucky underwear'.
sentences.chinese: 而且在世界的不同地方，总是有人对他们的“幸运内裤”深信不疑。

sentences.english: The bottom line is that you need to study, sleep well on the eve of the test, eat a nutritious meal, drink plenty of water and believe that your efforts will pay off.
sentences.chinese: 最重要是你需要学习，在考试前夕睡个好觉，吃一顿有营养的饭，多喝水，并且相信你的努力会有回报。
